Subject: Observability watchbook & concrete plan for the ACME trial (SE session notes)

Hi Samir / Elena —

Great to meet on the SE deep-dive yesterday. Below is a concise POC observability plan including the dashboards, traces, log export paths, sample queries, and owner recommendations. 

High-level intent: give ACME end-to-end visibility into user-facing latency, model behavior (quality regressions), and cost drivers so you can sign off against the success criteria.

A) Dashboards (will provision Grafana dashboards in the trial tenant):
  1) API Latency dashboard
     - Metrics: p50/p95/p99 request latency, tail latency split by model variant, per-endpoint QPS
     - Panels: histogram of response size, time-series of rolling p95, heatmap of latency by hour
  2) Token economics dashboard
     - Metrics: tokens generated, tokens ingested, per-token cost, estimated hourly spend, cumulative spend vs budget
  3) Error & reliability dashboard
     - Metrics: 5xx rate, model fallback rate, infra OOMs, request timeouts
  4) Model quality & eval dashboard
     - Metrics: batch eval accuracy (ACME eval set), BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, sample failure cases (linked)
  5) KV cache / prefix-hit dashboard
     - Metrics: KV cache hit rate, average KV hit latency, cache eviction rate

B) Tracing and root-cause artifacts:
  - Distributed traces instrumented for request-id (open telemetry). Key spans: client ingress, request-router, model-infer, kv-lookup, encode/decode.
  - Sentry/stackdriver alerts for uncaught exceptions and large tail latencies.

C) Logs & export:
  - Structured JSON logs with fields: request_id, model, span_durations_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, user_id (hashed), error_code
  - Exports: daily push to ACME S3 bucket (s3://acme-redwood-poc/logs/) and a Drive folder with sample queries.
  - Sample query file attached: sample_log_queries.txt

D) Success criteria mapping (how we'll measure automatically):
  - Latency: p95 payload latency < 300ms across trial window (dashboard alert triggers if 5-minute rolling p95 > 320ms)
  - Quality: nightly batch eval job against ACME eval set; pass if >=85% on the agreed metric
  - Cost: automated token-spend alert at 70% of budget and at 100% (hard stop configurable)

E) Ownership & runbook (recommended):
  - Dashboard owner (Redwood): Marissa Cole — provisioning, alert tuning, support during trial
  - App owner (ACME): Elena Ruiz — validation of quality metrics and sample cases
  - Escalation contact (Redwood): Jordan Blake — SLA & procurement questions
  - Billing / quota owner (Redwood): Rishi Malhotra — set spend limits and quota enforcement

F) Timeline (draft) — see attached spreadsheet but summarized:
  - Week 0 (this week): tenant + dashboards provisioned; test traces enabled
  - Week 1: trial ramp to 250 QPS; nightly eval running; tune caching
  - Week 2: ramp to target QPS (1k), run stress window, collect final eval results
  - End of Week 3: go/no-go decision meeting

G) Ask of ACME this week:
  - Upload eval set to Drive (Samir)
  - Provide S3 write credentials for log export or confirm Redwood-managed export location
  - Confirm procurement constraints (budget hard cap / sign-off owner)

I attached the watchbook and sample queries. Marissa will provision the dashboards by tomorrow and share links.

Cheers,

--
Marissa Cole
